covered.source: Ubuntu security notices (advisories that name a version)

gaps.why: needs an image scanner (trivy) and a vulnerability database; v0.2
gaps.consequence: a rebuilt image is reported as 'an update exists', never as 'these CVEs are fixed'
gaps.next: the real fix is outside this pane: rebuild the image on a schedule, because a base-image CVE is only fixed by a newer base. Scanning inside layers needs an image scanner (trivy), which 0.1.0 deliberately does not ship. Until then the digest check still tells you a newer build exists.

gaps.gap: language packages outside the global trees
gaps.why: cve_libraries reads the machine-wide installs it can list: npm's global tree, the first pip on PATH, composer's global vendor, local gems, cargo's installed binaries, dotnet's global tools, Maven's local repository, and Go's installed binaries. Per-project dependency files (package-lock.json, composer.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, *.csproj) and other virtualenvs are not read.
gaps.consequence: a vulnerable dependency of one project can be invisible while the machine-level list is clean
gaps.next: name the project in chat and I will query OSV for its packages ('which of my node/python dependencies have known CVEs in ~/projects/x?'). Reading lockfiles automatically is a 0.2 item; today it is one question away.

gaps.why: the vendor-lag comparison needs an advisory source that names a fixed version per release. Only Ubuntu's notice feed is wired, so a Fedora, Debian, Arch or openSUSE host reports a fix the archive does not carry as '0 pending'. Its bundled libraries are still read by cve_libraries.
gaps.consequence: on a non-Ubuntu host, 'nothing to do' can still mean 'the vendor has not shipped it yet'
gaps.next: one feed per distro would close it (Fedora's Bodhi, Debian's tracker API). Until then the gap is named here rather than implied by a green row.

gaps.why: adapters exist for: apt, dnf, pacman, zypper; every other OS answers 'unsupported' with its own id. Not implemented: Alpine (the apk adapter is written but has never read a real host), macOS, and Windows (which needs a PowerShell transport, not a package-manager block)
gaps.consequence: such a host is a red gap in this list, never a green 'patched'
gaps.next: nothing to switch on here: that host answers 'unsupported' on purpose, because reporting it as patched would be a guess. Measuring it means adding an adapter — a code change, not a setting. Until then use the distro's own updater, and open an issue with the distro id from cve_coverage.

coverage.note: the gap list is never empty and never green: an empty list would be a claim that nothing is missed

vulnerable.summary: Apache Log4j Core: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters
Apache Log4j Core: `verifyHostName` attribute silently ignored in TLS configuration
Incomplete fix for Apache Log4j vulnerability
vulnerable.severity: high (availability impact on a network service)
vulnerable.workaround: Log4j 2.16.0 fixes this issue by removing support for message lookup patterns and disabling JNDI functionality by default. This issue can be mitigated in prior releases (< 2.16.0) by removing the JndiLookup class from the classpath (example: zip -q -d log4j-core-*.jar org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class). Log4j 2.15.0 restricts JNDI LDAP lookups to localhost by default. Note that previous mitigations involving configuration such as to set the system property `log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups` to `true` do NOT mitigate this specific vulnerability.
